novelty.justification: The claim's wording—“LLMs exhibit a curse of knowledge” and teaching is “causally gated” by a “locatable and steerable” learner model—pursues both a new phenomenon in LLM explanation behavior and a new mechanistic account/measurement, rather than merely proposing personalized tutoring. The closest prior work is “Utility-based Adaptive Teaching Strategies using Bayesian Theory of Mind” (2023), which already constructs learner-state models and shows that learner-aware teacher agents outperform learner-agnostic ones; related searches used “curse of knowledge LLM teaching,” “LLM audience design learner model,” “predict then teach theory of mind language model,” “causal steering learner representation LLM,” and “Do LLMs mentalize when they teach.” The step from that work to this claim is a substantive but fairly natural extension/adaptation: it transfers Bayesian learner modeling into LLM hidden states and adds a causal localization-and-steering hypothesis, while the probe and steering techniques themselves are standard mechanistic-interpretability methods; therefore the core direction is more than a direct object swap but does not establish a wholly new paradigm, warranting a standard-to-high novelty score rather than 7–8.
